decisions_requested.title: WoodSpring Plainfield / Extended Stay America Plainfield

proposed_action.lineage: preserve 'woodspring suites indianapolis plainfield' as the superseded former identity; do not delete it from lineage

first_party_evidence: ESA property page names 6295 Gateway Dr, 46168 — the census address exactly (read 2026-08-31, free).
ESA page telephone 317-837-2950; page title 'Indianapolis - Plainfield'.
WoodSpring's OWN Indiana directory (woodspring.com) lists exactly THREE Indianapolis properties — Castleton, Airport South, Zionsville. Plainfield is NOT among them.
That directory is demonstrably current and complete: it correctly lists the two WoodSpring properties our census also holds, so the omission is an absence, not a directory failure.

ALREADY-OWNED evidence: the discovery-attempt ledger records a Google Places lookup for 'WoodSpring Suites Indianapolis Plainfield, 6295 Gateway Drive' (PTF-INDIANAPOLIS-PLACES-BROADER-RECOVERY-010, 2026-08-27) which returned UNBOUND_NO_SANCTIONED_KEY — no place matched that brand at that address.
hard_matching_signals: the former brand no longer claims the building, on the brand's own inventory
a second, independent source (Places, already paid for) also could not find the former brand there
conflicting_signals: brand name differs — which is exactly what a rebrand produces, and is the reason this was held rather than auto-merged
no telephone or property code comparison was possible: the census row carries NEITHER a phone nor a URL, so the strongest per-property signal is unavailable on our side
the census row came from OpenStreetMap, which lags rebrands by design; that explains the stale name but is not itself proof
decisions_requested.recommendation: APPROVE as a rebrand successor. Three independent sources agree the building at 6295 Gateway Dr is now ESA and is no longer WoodSpring. Treating it as two identities would publish a hotel that does not exist.
decisions_requested.census_impact: count UNCHANGED. One row is renamed and routed in place; nothing is added or retired.
decisions_requested.route_impact: +1 route at $0. The row leaves the 118-row unrouted cohort's IDENTITY_REVIEW_FIRST segment and becomes acquisition-ready with a first-party URL already in hand.
decisions_requested.publication_impact: NONE today. The row still has no policy evidence and publishes nothing until a policy is acquired and founder-approved.
decisions_requested.reversibility_note: Fully reversible: the superseded name is preserved in lineage and the route can be withdrawn. No published profile depends on it.

decisions_requested.title: Extended Stay America Castleton — address discrepancy

proposed_action.verdict: A. the census identity is correct but its ADDRESS IS STALE
proposed_action.lineage: record 8280 Bash Street as the superseded historical address with its provenance; do NOT erase it

first_party_evidence: ESA's own Indianapolis directory lists exactly ONE Castleton property, and its page names 7940 N. Shadeland Ave., 46250 (read 2026-08-31, free).

ALREADY-OWNED evidence: the discovery ledger records a Places lookup for 'Extended Stay America Indianapolis Castleton, 8280 Bash Street' (PTF-INDIANAPOLIS-PLACES-QUALIFICATION-008, 2026-08-27) returning UNBOUND_NO_SANCTIONED_KEY — nothing was findable under that name at that address.
The census row carries no URL and no telephone, and its provenance is PRIOR_CENSUS — the weakest source class in this market.

Bash Street is a genuine hotel cluster (the census holds Comfort Inn 8330, Quality Inn 8380, WoodSpring 8255), so this is NOT a case of one street with one building; the specific claim that an ESA sits at 8280 is what no source supports.
7940 N. Shadeland Ave appears nowhere in the census, so nothing else already holds the real address.
hard_matching_signals: ESA operates exactly one property in Castleton, so 'the ESA in Castleton' denotes one building and only one
conflicting_signals: street does NOT agree (8280 Bash St vs 7940 N. Shadeland Ave), and the two are about half a mile apart

we cannot prove from free sources that an ESA ever stood at 8280 Bash Street; the alternative reading — an ESA that closed there, plus a separate current one on Shadeland — is not excluded by the evidence we have
no telephone or property code exists on our side to bind with
decisions_requested.recommendation: APPROVE the address supersession, and note the residual doubt. This is the reading that cannot create a phantom: superseding corrects one row to the only ESA Castleton that demonstrably exists. Admitting 7940 N. Shadeland as a SECOND row would assert two ESA Castletons, which ESA's own inventory contradicts. If you prefer maximum caution, the alternative is to leave the row unrouted and admit nothing — that costs one route and one likely pet-friendly profile.
decisions_requested.census_impact: count UNCHANGED. One row's address and URL are corrected in place.
decisions_requested.route_impact: +1 route at $0; the row leaves IDENTITY_REVIEW_FIRST.
decisions_requested.publication_impact: NONE today. No policy evidence exists for it yet.
decisions_requested.reversibility_note: Reversible: the old address is preserved in lineage and can be restored. Nothing published depends on it.

decisions_requested.title: ZIPs 46236 and 46239 — three approved identities with no corridor
decisions_requested.current_state: Three identities you approved under COVERAGE-001 are withheld from the census because their ZIPs belong to no declared Indianapolis corridor, and this market requires every census row to resolve to exactly one corridor.

candidates.area: Geist / German Church Road, north-east Marion County

why: All three properties state their own city as Indianapolis on their own brand pages.

The market contract defines this market as 'the Indianapolis visitor market, not municipal limits and not the entire MSA', and enumerates its exclusions explicitly: Zionsville, Anderson, Muncie, Bloomington, Columbus IN, Lafayette, Terre Haute, Richmond, Kokomo, Shelbyville, Greenfield beyond the east I-70 corridor, and the Cincinnati-owned south-east. Neither 46236 nor 46239 is excluded, and neither is a named outer destination.

Both ZIPs are interior to the existing footprint rather than beyond it: 46236 sits between declared 46256 (keystone-castleton) and declared 46235 (east-i70); 46239 sits between declared 46229 (east-i70) and declared 46237 (south).
These are therefore corridor GAPS inside the market, not an expansion of it. Neither creates an isolated island.
geography_findings.not_a_count_argument: This is not recommended in order to raise the hotel count. Three hotels is immaterial to the 56 published; the reason to resolve it is that the market currently has holes its own boundary note does not intend.

options.mechanism: add the three identity keys to explicit_hotel_ids on the nearest corridor — 46236 to indianapolis-in__keystone-castleton, 46239 to indianapolis-in__east-i70
options.precedent: this is exactly how five existing census rows in ZIPs 46202 and 46222 are already assigned; the market contract's boundary note documents the pattern ('Shared ZIP 46202 is not registered to any corridor; those properties are assigned explicitly')
options.admits: exactly these three and nothing else
options.risk: none of the ZIP is swept in, so a future hotel in 46236/46239 returns to you rather than being auto-admitted
options.corridor_pages_changed: none created; two existing corridors each gain hotels

options.mechanism: add 46236 to keystone-castleton and 46239 to east-i70 included_postal_codes
options.admits: these three AND every future hotel discovered in those ZIPs, automatically
options.risk: a standing geography decision made once, applied silently thereafter; also a thematic stretch — Pendleton Pike is not Keystone, and Brookville Crossing is not I-70

options.admits: these three, with navigable neighbourhood pages
options.risk: creates corridor pages carrying 1-2 hotels each; the market's smallest existing corridor (mass-ave) carries 1, so this is permitted but thin

options.admits: nothing; the three approved identities stay out of the census permanently

decisions_requested.recommendation: Option 1, explicit assignment. It admits exactly what you already approved, uses a mechanism this market already relies on, changes no published page structure, and leaves the ZIP-level geography decision open rather than settling it silently for every future hotel.
decisions_requested.census_impact: +3 identities (shadow 265 -> 268). Pinned census unchanged either way.
decisions_requested.route_impact: +3 rows to the unrouted cohort (118 -> 121). All three arrive with a first-party URL already known, so they are routing-cheap.
decisions_requested.publication_impact: NONE today — no policy evidence. If later published they would appear under the assigned corridor.
decisions_requested.reversibility_note: Reversible. Explicit assignment is a list entry that can be removed; no published profile depends on it.

findings_reported_not_asked.why_it_survived: the Places bind for this row succeeded on NAME_AND_POSTAL_CODE, which never compares the street — so a wrong street passes a successful bind.

findings_reported_not_asked.finding: Census rows sourced from PRIOR_CENSUS bind to Google Places at 19 of 82 (23%), against 24 of 61 (39%) for rows from other sources. All three address discrepancies found in this work order are PRIOR_CENSUS rows.
findings_reported_not_asked.caveat: an UNBOUND result does not by itself prove a wrong address — the bind requires a sanctioned key and can fail on the name alone. This is a correlation worth investigating, not a proven defect count.
findings_reported_not_asked.recommended: a separate zero-cost work order to re-verify PRIOR_CENSUS addresses against brand first-party pages. Explicitly NOT actioned here.
